sections.h2: Where do Washington County owners go in Chipley for property tax questions?
sections.html:
Three separate offices in Chipley handle a Washington County parcel, and each answers a different question. The property appraiser sets value and takes exemption filings at 850-638-6205. The tax collector sends the bill and accepts payment at 1331 S. Blvd #101 (mailed payments go to PO Box 1038) and is staffed Monday through Friday, eight to four Disputes land with the circuit clerk's board records desk at 1293 Jackson Avenue, Suite 101.

The appraiser's FAQ describes the November bill as a relay. One office prices every parcel at its January 1 market level, each taxing body then chooses a rate to fund its budget, and a third office mails the result. The appraiser never levies or collects anything. Calling the wrong desk costs a day, so pick the office before you dial.

  • Parcel value, ownership records, exemption filings: property appraiser.
  • Balance owed, the installment plan, certificates: tax collector, 850-638-6275.
  • Petitions about a value or a refused exemption: the board's clerk, 850-638-6233.

sections.h2: Which levies stack up on a Washington County tax bill?
sections.html:
Seven rate lines appear on the collector's 2026 millage page, and just two belong to towns. Chipley and Vernon charge their own rates, so land outside both towns has no municipal line. The county line comes from the five-member commission, one seat per district, while the school board and the regional water district control the rest.

sections.h2: Which months drive the Washington County tax calendar?
sections.html:
The collector's deadline page opens with a discount and closes with a penalty. Payment made after March 31 counts as late.

  • November: collection starts, and paying by the 30th earns the largest discount, 4 percent.
  • December: the discount drops to 3 percent.
  • January: 2 percent.
  • February: 1 percent.
  • March 31: the full gross amount.
  • April 1: delinquency begins; real property takes a 3 percent penalty and business equipment starts accruing monthly interest.
  • Within 45 days: delinquent parcels run in a local newspaper, and the printing charge joins the balance.

The appraiser's calendar sits upstream. Value and residency are fixed on January 1, personal exemption filings run through March 1, the TRIM notice lands in August, and the board petition window shuts in September.

sections.h2: Can a Washington County owner pay in four installments?
sections.html:
Yes, and the collector lists each date. The first payment is due by June 1, and a participant who has not paid it by June 30 is dropped. Number two follows before September 30, number three by December 31, and the last by March 31. Current participants stay enrolled without reapplying.

New applications for the following year close April 30, a day earlier than the state's May 1 cutoff described on the Department of Revenue taxpayer page. Owners whose lender escrows the taxes gain nothing from it, since the lender settles the whole bill in November.

sections.h2: What happens to a Washington County parcel when a tax certificate is sold?
sections.html:
Someone else pays your late tax and gets a lien in return, with no claim to the land itself. The collector's page says the sale starts by June 1 for the previous year's unpaid real estate tax, after a three week newspaper notice.

The certificate amount adds the unpaid tax, any non ad valorem assessments, the penalty, a five percent commission for the collector and ad costs. Bids open at 18 percent interest and fall; the lowest bid wins, and that rate is what you pay to redeem. Where the earned interest would fall short of five percent, a five percent minimum is charged.

Two details involve small balances and old liens. Homestead land with a face amount below $250 skips the public sale, and the county holds that certificate at 18 percent. Every certificate dies after seven years. The collector accepts only certified funds in US dollars to redeem, and warns that missing the 22 month redemption period can end in a tax deed sale. A link to an online sale site sits on the collector's front page.

sections.h2: What does the Washington County appraiser want to see for a homestead claim?
sections.html:
The appraiser's exemption page lists a homestead benefit of up to $50,722, claimed in person on Form DR-501 before the March 1 cutoff. A flat $25,000 hits every levy, schools included. The page puts the second layer at up to $25,722 for 2025; it sits on value above $50,000, excludes school taxes, and is complete at $75,000 of assessed value.

The appraiser treats residency as a finding of fact, weighing your statements, workplace, voter registration, license, vehicle tags and the address on your federal return. Bring the following:

  • A recorded deed or a bill in your name, and a Social Security number for each owner.
  • Florida driver licenses for you and a spouse.
  • A Washington County voter card or a Declaration of Domicile, plus Florida registrations for every vehicle you own.
  • The trust agreement, if a trust holds title.
  • For a mobile home, the title or registration; you must also own the ground under it.

Spouses together get a single exemption. Skipping March 1 forfeits that year, although a late application can be taken to the Value Adjustment Board.

sections.h2: Which extra breaks does the Washington County appraiser list?
sections.html:
The page names several smaller breaks, some with conditions that matter at a sale.

  • Senior break: up to $50,000 more for a homestead owner who turned 65 by January 1, if household income stays under a ceiling that began at $20,000 and rises with a cost of living index. It touches county millage only and needs a sworn income statement by March 1.
  • Five thousand dollars each for unremarried widows and widowers, total and permanent disability, blindness, and veterans with at least a 10 percent service disability.
  • Full exemption for an honorably discharged veteran who is totally and permanently disabled through service; it may pass to a surviving spouse.
  • A granny flat reduction, limited to 20 percent of assessed value, for permitted quarters housing a parent or grandparent who is 62 or older.

Each one ends or must be refiled when ownership changes, so a buyer begins with nothing.

sections.h2: How does a Washington County owner challenge a value or a missed exemption?
sections.html:
Ask the board for a hearing by petition, delivered to the clerk. The clerk's page sends you to the appraiser (850-638-6205) or the board clerk (850-638-6233) for the cutoff date, and the appraiser's FAQ says it usually falls in early September.

The clerk lists several rules. A $50 fee is charged and not refunded, except for appeals of a timely homestead denial or a deferral denial. The state form must be printed and carry an original signature, since copies and faxes are turned away. A representative needs written authority from the owner, and a late filing needs written reasons for good cause.

Talk to an appraiser first. The office walks through each property at least every third year, adjusts values between visits when sales shift, and will show the data behind a figure. Its FAQ defines a usable sale as one between a willing buyer and seller under no pressure, so a below-market family transfer does not move the market. Non-homestead assessments cannot climb more than 10 percent annually, so a larger leap on a rental or empty lot suggests new building or a sale.

sections.h2: What should a Washington County landlord or small business know about equipment tax?
sections.html:
Business and rental equipment sits on a separate account with separate penalties. Anyone holding such assets on January 1 files by April 1; the appraiser's FAQ says late returns draw 5 percent a month, capped at 25 percent. The collector adds its own monthly interest on delinquent equipment tax after April 1, begins warrant work May 1 and advertises the list once.

There is no reporting floor, and fully depreciated items still count. A business buyer inherits the tax, including any January 1 shortfall. A landlord selling a furnished rental should tell the appraiser so the account closes and no stray bill follows.

sections.h2: What should a Washington County seller with unpaid tax do before closing?
sections.html:
Get a payoff letter from the collector that runs through the closing day and pass it to the title agent. A sale before April 1 sidesteps the penalty and the ad charge. Deed stamps cost seventy cents per hundred dollars of price outside Miami-Dade, and the Department of Revenue holds every signer liable, so name the payer in the contract.

Do not expect the seller's bill to repeat. The state's Save Our Homes guide says the cap lapses with a sale and value jumps to market the next January 1.

faqs.q: What date makes a Chipley area tax bill late?
faqs.a: April 1. That day the collector attaches a 3 percent penalty to real property and starts monthly interest on business equipment.

faqs.q: How much do I save by paying in January?
faqs.a: Two percent off. The collector's list steps down from 4 percent in November through 3, 2 and 1 in the following months.

faqs.q: Could a tiny balance cost someone a homestead?
faqs.a: Not through a public sale at first. A homestead lien under $250 is issued to the county at 18 percent and can be sold to a buyer only after the amount plus interest passes $250.

faqs.q: How long does a certificate stay alive?
faqs.a: Seven years, counted from the sale's opening day. The owner's redemption window is 22 months under the period the collector cites.

faqs.q: Where can I read the latest rate lines?
faqs.a: On the collector's millage page, which prints seven 2026 lines. The page does not call them adopted, so phone 850-638-6275 to confirm.
